card: Validates numeric configuration arguments at startup, rejecting negative or out-of-range inputs instead of allowing silent wrapping or fallback. Options including -dbbatchsize, mempool limits, network buffer sizes, and timeouts now cause an explicit error on invalid values. The author notes that a negative -dbbatchsize previously wrapped to an immense value and disabled flushing, risking unbounded memory usage during reindex. The change also updates -help text for several arguments to indicate their value placeholder.
evidence: PR description and commit message: "A negative `-dbbatchsize` wrapped to a huge value and disabled batch flushing, so a reindex could hold an unbounded batch in memory."
PR description: "`-timeout` must be positive. It previously fell back to the default silently, unlike the analogous `-peertimeout`, which already errored."
problem: Passing negative or out-of-range numbers to several configuration options causes unintended behavior such as integer wrapping or silent fallbacks. For instance, a negative -dbbatchsize wraps to an enormous unsigned integer, disabling batch flushing and allowing reindex operations to accumulate unbounded memory.

risk.why: A bug or over-restrictive range check in argument parsing could cause existing node configurations to fail to start.

scope_notes: The diff was not provided, but the change spans 11 files, likely touching option registration and parsing across network, mempool, validation, and database initialization.
summary: Validates numeric command-line and configuration file arguments during initialization, rejecting negative or out-of-bounds values. Settings covering database flushing, mempool cluster and ancestor limits, network buffers, ban time, and connection timeouts now raise startup errors rather than wrapping or silently falling back. The change also updates -help descriptions for several options to display their required value placeholder.
uncertainties: The diff was omitted, so the exact error handling implementation and touched files could not be directly verified.
